title: fix(plugin-audit)!: seal a window into checkpoints of at most 10,000 rows, and bound the idle re-walk (P4b2)
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-elon-musk"} -->
_Requested by **Elon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D?thread=cmsg_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9DXuamRUC67fx2TTYrFfyuSH)_

Part of #31908 (slice P4b2)
Blocked-by: #33489 (governed ADR-0154 amendment; merged to `main` as 8f915f2a1, which this branch now contains)

Clause-②: yes (narrowing) — narrowed: `os audit verify` reports a row id that two checkpoints list as the new chain fault `listed_twice` and fails the run, where the 18.4.0 verifier accepted it, and the 18.4.0 sealer could write such a chain when two of its late sealings overlapped. Widened: two optional signed-body fields (`part_index`, `final_part`), two nullable `sys_audit_checkpoint` columns for them, and the `AuditChainFaultKind` member `listed_twice`.
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: follow-up #33773 — skills/objectstack-data/evals/objects-fields-relationships.json, skills/objectstack-data/rules/lifecycle.md — both still teach that the sealer signs each `created_at` hour into one checkpoint per organization, where this change cuts a window into checkpoints of at most 10,000 rows each (the eval's graded `expected_output`, and `lifecycle.md` § Sealing); the card also carries their older stale claim that no verifier exists, which `os audit verify` already contradicts. `skills/**` is changed only on a `domain:skills` PR, so this one does not edit them; `content/docs/data-modeling/objects.mdx` and `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx` gain the parts, the new fault and what a removed checkpoint shows in this change.

**BREAKING** for `os audit verify` on a chain that an 18.4.0 sealer wrote while two of its late sealings overlapped (two replicas with no cluster service, whose lock is in-process only, or a lease that lapsed). Such a chain lists one late row in two checkpoints. Verify now reports it as `listed_twice` and fails, where it passed. No tolerance and no repair ships for it (seat ruling 6888674846 item 1). A chain one sealer wrote at a time is not affected. ADR-0087 disposition, in the changeset: `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. `@objectstack/plugin-audit` stays `patch`, because `Metadata-protocol: none`.

## Maintainer quick read

- **What changed:** the audit sealer now seals each organization's hour of audit rows into checkpoints of at most 10,000 rows each, instead of one checkpoint of any size. `os audit verify` now fails when two checkpoints list the same row. While one organization's chain is stuck, a pass stops re-reading old windows after 168 windows that seal nothing, and once no chain is stuck the walk is not cut, so sealing catches up.
- **Why:** one busy hour made one huge checkpoint, so the work and memory of a single seal grew without limit. And while one chain stayed stuck on a bad row, every hourly pass re-read every row since that window. Seat ruling 6884540128 item 1 (S7) and review#3 S1 on #33503 ask for both bounds.
- **Risk and rollback:** this changes how new checkpoints are cut, not the insert path. Checkpoints written before this release still verify, as one final part. Upgrading is one way once this release writes a checkpoint: an 18.4.0 verifier fails the signature of every checkpoint that carries the two new fields, and an 18.4.0 sealer's next checkpoint is a `link` fault. No object opts into sealing by default, so this only matters for an app that declared `lifecycle.seal`.
- **Look first:** `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/sealer.ts` (the walk in `run` and what counts toward the idle cap, the S1 re-check in `writeCheckpoint`, `writeChain`, `leavesOf`), then `signed-body.ts` (`checkpointPartOf` and the part docblocks), then `verifier.ts` (`listed_twice` in `judgeCheckpoint`).
- **Two-minute check:** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-audit exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/audit-seal/audit-seal-sealer.test.ts`: expect 52 passed, including the "bounded checkpoints" and "uncounted re-walk" groups.
- **What you need to do:** nothing: #33489 has merged, and the seat lands this once review passes.

## What changes

**S7: bounded checkpoints (ADR-0154 D4 as amended in #33489).**
- A chain's window seals into consecutive checkpoints of at most `AUDIT_SEAL_MAX_LEAVES = 10_000` leaves. N is a fixed exported constant, not a knob. The internal `AuditSealerOptions.maxLeaves` is a test seam beside `now`. `AuditPlugin` never passes it, and the sealer is not exported from the package.
- Parts are cut in D1 order, `(created_at, id)`, and each part's leaves are in that order. Each part draws its own seed (D2), so one seed still covers one checkpoint.
- A window is read twice: once for each row's id and canonical `created_at`, then each part's rows by id, in `$in` batches of 500, hashed under that part's seed. So one checkpoint's hashing, ids, body and memory are bounded by N. A row deleted or moved between the two reads is left out of its part.
- The signed body gains `part_index` (from 0) and `final_part`. `sys_audit_checkpoint` stores them in two new nullable columns.
- Resume: a chain whose newest `window` checkpoint is not final resumes that window as further `window` parts. They continue its part count and seal only rows no checkpoint lists yet. They are never sealed as `late`.
- `late` sealings split the same way. A late part's index counts within that one late sealing (the prose line for this is on #33489, seat ruling 6888674846 item 2).
- The sealer's S1 check ("not sealed twice") is relaxed for parts. A `window` part is refused when the chain already holds a later window, a part of this window at this index or past it, or a checkpoint of this window written before the amendment (NULL part index).
- `os audit verify` faults a row id that two checkpoints list, as the new fault kind `listed_twice`. The second listing holds nothing for that row.
- Compatibility: a checkpoint with neither field (written before this release, NULL columns) reads back without them. Its signed bytes are unchanged, so it verifies and reads as one final part. A body with one field and not the other is refused.

**What verify does and does not see of a removed part (seat ruling 6888674846 item 3).** Verify adds no continuity check and no final-part check. The chain links expose a removed *interior* part, as a `gap` or a `link` fault. They do not see a removed *newest* part; its rows are reported as late and unsealed instead, because a surviving part of the same window still names that window as sealed. A final part cannot be required, because `writeChain` skips a part whose rows all went between the two reads: `part_index` can then skip a number, and a window whose last part emptied has no final part.

**review#3 S1: bounded idle re-walk.** The separate cap `AUDIT_SEAL_MAX_IDLE_WINDOWS_PER_PASS` (168, one late horizon of windows) counts windows that seal nothing, and only while a chain is skipped in the pass. A pass that has walked that many stops walking, and the sealer reports it at `error`, naming the skipped chains. With no chain skipped the walk is not cut, so it reaches the next window that seals something and the floor moves past the rest.

Why the cap and not the seek. Seeking from the minimum per-chain cursor is only correct if the sealer knows every chain that still has rows. Per-chain cursors exist only for chains with a `window` checkpoint at or past the floor. Two kinds of chain are missing from that set:
- a chain skipped at a later window than the one holding the floor;
- a chain with no checkpoint since the floor.

Neither is recorded anywhere durable. A seek would pass over their windows, and once the floor moved their on-time rows would seal as `late`. That breaks S4's rule that a skipped chain resumes "from its own oldest unsealed window" as `window` checkpoints. The cap never changes how a row seals, only when. Its cost: after about a week of a chain that stays skipped, chains past the cap wait for it, and that is loud.

The window-major pin and the no-late-sweep pin from P4b1 are unchanged and green.

**Docs.** `content/docs/data-modeling/objects.mdx` said each hour seals into one checkpoint per organization; it now says one checkpoint, or consecutive checkpoints of at most 10,000 rows. `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx` gains what verify shows of a removed checkpoint, and its exit code 1 entry now names a row that two checkpoints list.

**Spec.** The signed body is declared in `plugin-audit` (`audit-seal/signed-body.ts`), not in `packages/spec`. There is no Zod schema, generated JSON schema or reference doc for it, so nothing in spec is regenerated.

## Round 2: what each item of review#3 got

- **M1** (ff13294f): the changeset and this body declare `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, carry the BREAKING banner, and the changeset holds one ADR-0087 marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, stating that a chain sealed by 18.4.0 with overlapping late sealers now reports `listed_twice`. `Metadata-protocol: none`, so `patch`. No tolerance or heal code.
- **M2** (6bb7f490, ff13294f, this body): the wording above, in the `part_index` / `final_part` docblocks and in the changeset. Pinned: a removed interior part is a `gap`, and a removed newest part reads unsealed with no chain fault.
- **N1** (ff13294f): the one-way upgrade note is in the changeset.
- **N2** (6bb7f490): the S1 re-check's `$or` gains `{ window_start in this window, part_index: { $null: true } }`. The seal-store testkit now judges a `where` as SQL does (a comparison with a NULL column is never true, and `$null` is `IS NULL`), so the pin is red without the arm.
- **N3** (b189644b, e9302166): the five pins asked for, plus an emptied middle part. See Tests.
- **N4** (6bb7f490): the `part_index` docblock says the count may skip an emptied part.
- **Found while pinning N3's last item, fixed here** (6bb7f490): the idle cap never let go. It counted every window that sealed nothing, skipped chain or not. Once the stuck chain was fixed, the windows the cap had left behind still counted, so the walk stopped short of the next window that seals something again. No checkpoint was written, the floor never moved, and the object never sealed past the cap. That held whether the stuck row was corrected in place or deleted. The cap now counts only while a chain is skipped in the pass.
- **Docs** (f08afcaff): the two pages above, which this PR had made false or incomplete, and the changeset's `Skills-docs:` line that the `(narrowing)` arm owes.
- The base moved to `main` after #33503 merged; `origin/main` is merged in (faadaaab, then 60960cd6a, which brings in #33489), and this PR's diff against `main` is P4b2 alone.
- b234eee59 (another agent, test-only): a 30 s budget on the three stalled-chain re-walk tests, after a Test Core timeout. The local runs below predate it.
- 5ef334ec merges `main` again (412fbf76b); the full dogfood battery at 5ef334ec ran green, 467 test files and 3958 tests. 55dfebcfc (review#3 record 6891899947, M1): the changeset's `Skills-docs:` line and this body's now name the filed follow-up card, #33773, in place of `follow-up owed` and `none`.

## Why

Seat ruling 6884540128 item 1 (S7), with the ADR-0154 amendment in #33489. review#3's should-fix S1 on #33503 (comment 6885454935). review#3 on this PR (comment 6888713592) and seat rulings 6888674846.

## Tests

Each new pin that covers new behaviour was run red before its fix.

Round 1: the pins were committed first (4827322fe), the implementation files were set back to the base, and the pins were run. 10 failed: the seven S7 sealer pins, the duplicate-id verifier pin, two signed-body pins, and the idle re-walk pin, which read **200** windows in one pass before the cap. The pin "a checkpoint written before the amendment still verifies" was run red against the first implementation, before the compatibility fix in 0dd58a80e.

Round 2: the pins were committed first (b189644b, then e9302166 for one precondition) and run against the round-1 implementation, on the tree merged with `main`:
- red: the pre-amendment S1 pin (`expected 1 to be +0`: a second `window` checkpoint listing `r1` was written);
- red: both re-seal pins after the idle cap, once the stuck row was fixed in place and once it was deleted (`expected [ 'a0', … (182) ] to deeply equal [ 'a0', … (197) ]`, and the same with 181 and 196: 15 of org_a's rows never sealed);
- green, as they pin behaviour round 1 already had: the tie across a part boundary, a row deleted or moved between the reads, an emptied middle part, an emptied last part and its resume, and the removed interior and newest parts.

New pins this round, in `audit-seal-sealer.test.ts`:
- A window part is refused beside a pre-amendment checkpoint of that window that another sealer wrote after this pass read the window (NULL part columns, re-signed without the keys); the error names the part, and the ledger verifies.
- A `created_at` tie that straddles a part boundary cuts the same way whichever order the rows were written in: the id decides the side.
- A row deleted, or moved to the next window, between the two reads is left out of its part; the moved row seals in its new window.
- A middle part that empties between the reads is skipped without taking its index: parts 0 and 2.
- A last part that empties leaves the window with no final part; the next pass writes nothing, and a row that arrives in that window afterwards is `window` part 1, final, never `late`.
- A removed interior part is a `gap` fault and its rows read unsealed; a removed newest part raises no chain fault and its rows read unsealed.
- After the idle cap was hit, the whole object seals again once the stuck chain's row is fixed in place, and once it is deleted: every row is listed exactly once, none as `late`, and the second case verifies ok.

## Acceptance notes

- **Part index of a `late` part** counts within the one late sealing that wrote it. A second late sealing of the same window starts at 0 again. Seat ruling 6888674846 item 2 accepts this; its prose line is on #33489.
- **A part whose rows all went** between the two reads is not written and takes no index, so `part_index` can skip a number. If that was the last part, the window has no final part; the next pass resumes it, and a row that arrives in it later seals as the next `window` part. Verify checks neither part continuity nor a final part. The chain links show a removed interior part as a `gap` or `link` fault; they do not show a removed newest part, whose rows read unsealed instead. When the removed checkpoint was the only one naming the object's newest window, that is ADR-0154's head truncation, which this check alone cannot see.
- **Rows moved between the two reads** (a changed `created_at` or `tenant_id`) are left out of the part. They are sealed later in their new window (as `late` if that window is already sealed), or the verifier reports them.
- **The S1 re-check against a pre-amendment checkpoint** matters only when a sealer of an earlier release runs beside this one during a rolling upgrade with no cluster lock; the unique `(sealed_object, chain_key, sequence)` index does not cover it, because the later pass reads the chain head after the other sealer's insert.
